doc_friction.issue: The session started already on the harness branch claude/cool-franklin-18vjc1; `git checkout -b` failed. Harmless, but the land-your-work steps assume you create it.

The proposal named a check valve as part of the fix; working the numbers showed a spring check valve (about 3 kPa to crack) would block a thermosiphon's few tens of pascals entirely, so the story turned the valve into the builder's wrong idea. Proposals that name a fix should have their fix checked too, not just the fault.

deviations.why: Proposal's fix included 'a one-way valve the old installer never needed' and a failed pump undone by 'the first cloudy week flattens the battery'. The model showed the timer pump does not do worse in cloudy weather than no pump, and a spring check valve would stop forward flow too.
deviations.did: Dropped the cloudy-week failure (the pump fails because mornings stay cold, which the model shows); made the check valve Rigoberto's idea, rejected with the numbers; the fix is the tank back on a stand ('the height is the valve').
deviations.result: Every number in the story comes from the note's model.

notes: Project hearth-and-horizon, piece the-tank-above-the-panel (Hearth & Horizon shelf, ~4,970 words, text only; audio dir total 577 MB). Claimed the proposal with a draft PR before drafting. Physics worked in a minute-step thermosiphon model (loop density integral, quasi-steady collector, mixed tank, fixed laminar resistance): stand 48.6 C at 06:00, plinth 23.4 C, plinth+timer pump 24.9 C, plinth with valve shut overnight 44.8 C; ~6.3 kWh/night reverse loss. An adversarial re-read caught: wrong weekdays for half the dates (rechecked with datetime), a noon drain-cock test where the model tank was only 32 C (moved to 16:00), 7 vs 7.6 reams, an unnecessary tinaco raise, an unchecked 'morning star' for 2047. Added a timeline row and a new H&H proposal (rammed earth; H&H Next up was otherwise empty). Local: node --test in ventures/hearth-and-horizon 20/20 pass.
